messages:
maria-chen: observed a 10-15% P50 increase on host ingress over the last 3 deploys. attaching the short flame and a small trace. can we sync?
kevin-zhou: thanks. any immediate suspects? kernel selection, batching, or kvcache?
samuel: I threw a lightweight perf run — looks like stalls inside the parse pipeline while waiting on a small KV eviction loop. spike correlates with hs_tokenizer allocations.
maria-chen: here's the quick trace snippet:
```
host_parse() -> tokenize_stream() -> kv_cache.get_or_evict() -> token_emit()
--- wait 12-18ms in kv_cache.free_path when sequence len is ~512
```
kevin-zhou: interesting. kernel choice should be irrelevant that deep in the ingest path. suspects: tokenizer backpressure + synchronous KV free path.
jamal: I saw similar on canary on thursday. HTTP/2 WINDOW_UPDATE bursts caused batching watermark to drop to 1 and that exposed sync-free-paths.
runtime-bot: deploy 2965120000 to prod-stage finished. canary traffic at 5%
maria-chen: reproduced locally with the same load generator. enabling async_kv_free reduces p50 but adds a 0.5% p99 tail.
samuel: Can you paste the micro-benchmark?
maria-chen: micro-bench command: `./tools/bench_ingress --seq 512 --qps 200 --conn 50 --tokenize async_off`
kevin-zhou: patch idea: convert kv_cache.free_path to deferred free (queue + background batch free) and add a small prefetch hint in tokenizer to avoid touching eviction path during initial emit.
jamal: also consider batching heuristic tweak — increase batch fill threshold by 10% when host load > 70% so we don't prematurely flush small batches during HTTP/2 window pressure.
samuel: I prototyped deferred free. rough numbers: p50 down 12%, cpu overhead +2%, p99 regressed 0.7%. we probably need a better cluster sizing for background free workers.
maria-chen: attached perf counters: `cycles_stalled_backend` spikes during those eviction calls. stack: tokenize->kv->free->alloc->emit. Looks like allocator fragmentation too.
kevin-zhou: allocator + sync free path = bad combo. two incremental options: 1) move free to background, 2) use freelist pooling for small token buffers to avoid malloc churn. both can be gated behind a runtime flag.
jamal: for immediate mitigation, we should add a short-circuit in ingress: if batch_size <= 2 and connection window small then use small-copy path that avoids kv eviction entirely. cheaper than full async refactor and safe to canary.
maria-chen: agreed. i'll draft a tiny patch and add `--ingress-small-copy` flag. will also add telemetry for `kv_eviction_ms` and `token_allocs` metrics.
samuel: will bench that patch and check kernel dispatch telemetry — sometimes the runtime picks a wide-kernel for seq512 which increases memory traversal pressure; might be worth constraining kernel choice when host-side parse is hot.
kevin-zhou: good call. add a kernel-selection override tied to `ingress_parse_hot` metric so we avoid wide memory walks while host CPU is saturated.
maria-chen: sending PR now: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5142 includes deferred free flag + small-copy short-circuit + telemetry.
jamal: can we canary at 1% in prod-stage? runtime-bot please schedule. :thumbsup:
runtime-bot: canary scheduled: pr=5142 roll=prod-stage/1% start=2965432600
maria-chen: will follow up with perf dashboard snapshots in ~30m. thanks all for quick triage :rocket:
